findings.where: Nav binding strip, the logo lockup (home link), at both widths
findings.fault: The logo has been recoloured. The arches and the 'MMM INFRA' wordmark are pale canary on the maroon binding, where the logo has grey #404040 arches and a blue #0070C0 wordmark. The 'Moseley Infrastructure Advisory Services' line is also missing from the lockup. Mark does not hold a version in these colours and has not approved one.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo is the one fixed part of his brand. In this tile his own blue and grey appear nowhere, so the identity he would sign off on is not his logo's.

findings.where: Whole page: contact route and page end (no footer at either width; the 'Write to me' margin note is the only contact)
findings.fault: Mark's email address never appears as text. The only contact is a mailto link behind a handwritten 'Write to me', and the page stops after the motion sketch with no footer, even though the palette assigns Binding to 'nav, footer'.
findings.who_objects: A procurement officer at a development bank who wants to copy the address into a shortlist, a form or webmail. On a work machine with no default mail app the scribble does nothing they can use, and they cannot see who they would be writing to.

findings.where: First screen, desktop: the 'Write to me' note in the left margin
findings.fault: The one primary action is the lightest thing on the first screen. It is a small tilted scribble about 130 px wide in the margin, outweighed by the headline, the photo print, the aqueduct sketch and even the nav links. It also lines up with no line of the hero text it belongs to.
findings.who_objects: The visitor who has decided to get in touch. Their eye goes from the headline to the sketch and scrolls on into the tile without stopping at the action, which is the page's whole job for Mark.

findings.where: Motion sketch: what moves on arrival (the margin note writing itself in)
findings.fault: The only motion on arrival is the call to action writing itself in. So the first thing that moves is the text asking for something, which inverts the client's 'calm first' value of one quiet moment before any text asks. The aqueduct, which the opening is meant to build, stays still.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who asked for a calm opening and for the aqueduct to be built. A first visit that opens with a 'write to me' scribbling itself in reads as a nudge.

findings.where: Motion sketch panel: the 'Replay the note' button
findings.fault: The button replays the margin note, but at both widths the note is at the top of the page, several screens above the button. Pressing it animates something off screen, so the visitor sees nothing happen. The button is also styled as an underlined text link.
findings.who_objects: Mark, or anyone judging the tile, who presses Replay to see the pen stroke and gets no visible result. The button looks dead.

findings.where: Article specimen: the lecture row 'Streamlining the PPP Process… / Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF'
findings.fault: The row's bottom rule runs tight under the last line of both columns, so it reads as an underline under the title and under 'Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF' alike. The title itself is bold ballpoint, the same as a heading. A reader cannot tell which part is the link, or whether the row is a link at all.
findings.who_objects: A reader who wants Mark's lecture PDF. They have to hover around the row to find what is clickable, and this row is the article page's pattern for publications.

findings.where: Palette and use: 'Ballpoint' #1B2A6B against 'Light hand' #34407A (hero line 'Over 40 years…', the article's date line)
findings.fault: The two inks are near-identical navies. Side by side as swatches, and in use as asides beside body text, they read as one blue that is slightly off rather than as two roles, so the asides look like a printing slip.
findings.who_objects: A reader, who cannot see that the italic aside is meant to be quieter. Angélique, who has two blues to choose between with no visible difference.

findings.where: Pad texture: the double margin line, at both widths
findings.fault: The double margin line is drawn in a dark olive-brown, while the palette assigns 'Margin red' #B8322B to the margin. The signature mark of a legal pad, the red double rule, does not appear, so the paper reads as generic yellow lined stock.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who proposed the legal pad for its legal associations. The red margin is what makes the paper read as a lawyer's pad, and the tile contradicts its own palette.

findings.where: Hero sketch of the aqueduct under the intro
findings.fault: The sketch is the logo mark itself (the tapered band over three arches, in the same proportions) redrawn in ink with hatching added, not an aqueduct drawn freely on the pad. Its ends barely trail off, so it reads as an enlarged, altered logo.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose mark the brief says is never redrawn. A second, hatched version of it on the home page competes with the real logo in the nav.

findings.where: First screen, the italic line 'Over 40 years of international infrastructure experience.' (both widths)
findings.fault: A count of years is given a line of its own in the first screen, set as a second statement under the lead. It is a size claim rather than a checkable fact, and it competes with the lead's stronger, specific line about the World Bank's PPP Group.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank reader, who selects against terms of reference and discounts year counts. It also goes against the client's 'confident without big-firm claims' value.

findings.where: Article specimen: the handwritten pull quote 'Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on…'
findings.fault: On the article page Mark's hand sets a content quote, although the tile says the hand is for one note per view, the call to action. On a real article that has the margin note, two handwritten lines would compete. At 64 px line spacing the quote also breaks into widely spaced fragments, three lines on phone.
findings.who_objects: A reader, for whom the call to action stops being the one handwritten thing. Angélique, who gets no clear rule on when a post uses the hand.

findings.where: Hero headline and the desktop article title, where the type sits on the ruled feints
findings.fault: The headings are snapped to the 32 px rule grid. The hero's 64/64 headline has a feint running through the middle of each line, and the article title on desktop opens to 64 px leading, so its two lines read as separate lines rather than one heading.
findings.who_objects: A reader. The struck-through display lines look like a misprint, and the loose title weakens the heading on a page meant for reading.
